name: Zzz
baseMeaning: Three Zs representing sleep or snoring.
tldr: 💤 means sleep or being done for the night, often used playfully to close a chat or show extreme tiredness.

contextMeanings.meaning: 💤 directly says that the sender is asleep, falling asleep, or close to it.
At the end of a chat, 💤 means the sender is done for the night and closing the conversation.
💤 can joke that a meeting or activity is so boring that the sender wishes they were asleep.
contextMeanings.example: this meeting is putting me to sleep 💤

contextMeanings.meaning: In a relaxed work thread, 💤 playfully marks the end of the sender’s participation for the day.

platformNotes.note: 💤 works well in iMessage, especially at the end of a goodnight exchange. It gives the thread a playful, cartoon-like ending without requiring a formal farewell.
💤 is less dependable in Instagram direct messages than 😴 or 🥱. Use it when the conversation has already established a casual, sleepy tone rather than as a serious sign-off.
💤 is unusual among tired symbols because it can survive a relaxed work channel without looking overly dramatic. Its non-face design helps it read as playful exhaustion.
💤 fits naturally in WhatsApp goodnight messages and family threads. Because WhatsApp conversations often cross generations and time zones, the surrounding words matter more than the symbol alone.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users commonly recognize the three Zs as quick cartoon shorthand for sleep, exhaustion, or being completely done.
Millennials often use 💤 as a soft way to end a conversation, especially when the chat has already been affectionate and relaxed.
A Boomer who is less familiar with the internet shorthand may take 💤 more literally, reading it as snoring or a simple statement about sleep.

warnings.title: It can sound like a brush-off
warnings.description: Sending 💤 while the conversation is still open can be taken as a soft dismissal, even when you only mean that you are exhausted. Send a plain sentence or wait until the exchange has naturally ended.

seoDescription: What does 💤 mean? It marks sleep, being exhausted, or playfully ending the night, with repeated Zs showing you are really out.

longForm.overview:
💤 is easy to misread because the three Zs look like a sound effect, not a face. The sender usually means that they are asleep, done for the night, or too tired to continue. In a goodnight message, it simply closes the exchange. In a close coworker thread, “this meeting 💤” is usually playful despair, not a serious complaint. The emoji’s cartoon quality is the point: it keeps the message light.

What changes the meaning is placement and company. One 💤 after “goodnight” says “I’m asleep.” 💤💤💤 after a frustrating message says “I am really out” or “I am done with this.” Sending 💤 while a conversation is still active is different: the recipient may hear it as a soft brush-off. Compared with 😴, 💤 is more stylized and playful; 😪 is a gentler tired closer, while 🥱 points more directly to boredom. Match 💤 to a thread where that cartoon shorthand will land.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
💤 usually arrives at the end of a message when someone is ready to stop talking. “goodnight 💤” is the clearest use: it turns the sentence into a miniature going-to-bed scene. In a close friend thread, it can also be wishful thinking during an dull meeting or an argument the sender would rather leave.

💤💤💤 adds emphasis. It says the sender is not merely tired but deeply asleep, completely checked out, or finished with the subject. That stronger version is best among people who already trade playful tired messages. It works especially well after a frustrating announcement because it can turn irritation into a cartoonish “I am done with this.”
longForm.whenNotToUse:
The clearest misfire is sending 💤 while the conversation is still active. A recipient may understand the intended message as “I am exhausted,” but they may also hear “I am ending this now.” If the point is simply being tired, say that directly or choose 😪, which feels gentler.

Do not use 💤 when you need the other person to keep engaging, answer a question, or acknowledge something important. Match the symbol to the relationship too: playful cartoon exhaustion works in close friendships and relaxed coworker threads, while a stranger may interpret it as odd or abrupt. Even in work chat, save it for a thread where that humor already fits.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 💤 at the end of a friendly exchange, close the beat with 😴, return one 💤, or simply say goodnight. You can also use 💤💤💤 to show that their message made you laugh, especially when the thread already has that playful tired tone.

If 💤 appears in the middle of a conversation and feels like a dismissal, ask whether they meant they were tired or ready to stop. If you sent it after frustrating content, soften the ending with a short sentence such as “I am completely done with this one.” That preserves the joke while making clear that you are not rejecting the person.

faqs.question: What does 💤 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Usually that he is sleepy or done for the night. It is not inherently romantic; the surrounding message and your relationship determine whether it reads as a literal sign-off or playful banter.

faqs.question: Is 💤 flirty?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. 💤 is primarily about sleep, exhaustion, or closing the conversation, so it becomes flirty only when the rest of the message is affectionate.

faqs.question: What does 💤 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: It usually means the creator is exhausted, asleep, or dramatically ready to leave the conversation. Comments and captions can add a sarcastic meaning, so watch the wording around it.

faqs.question: Why do people send 💤💤💤?
faqs.answer: The repeated Zs intensify the joke: the sender is extremely tired, deeply asleep, or completely done with what they are discussing. It is more emphatic and playful than a single 💤.

conversationExamples.message: i’m going to sleep before this turns into a full night shift 💤
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is winding down the night without necessarily suggesting a romantic invitation. Reply warmly and let them rest.

conversationExamples.message: call me after lunch, i’ll be asleep by then 💤💤💤
conversationExamples.interpretation: The repeated Zs exaggerate how completely checked out the sender expects to be. Respond with a joke or adjust the call time.

conversationExamples.message: i’m finished with today’s report, brain is officially gone 💤
conversationExamples.interpretation: This playfully signals that the sender has completed their work and is done for the day. A brief goodnight works.

conversationExamples.message: goodnight everyone, going to bed before i start snoring 💤
conversationExamples.interpretation: 💤 adds comic exaggeration to an ordinary family goodnight. Reply with your own sleepy sign-off.
The sender is joking about being unable to sleep and probably wants company. Reply conversationally rather than treating it as a firm sign-off.
